clue.text: See 19
Wealthy types act fast to become corrupt

indicators.note: letters that become corrupt are spoilt and come out in a changed order

explanation.surface: Rich people move quickly to turn crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat cats is a scornful idiom for rich, privileged people, especially overpaid executives.

clue.text: Rarely in trouble, expert passing competition

indicators.note: a word in trouble is in disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert at passing the ball seldom gets into trouble in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay race each runner passes the baton on to the next member of the team.

clue.text: Odd characters from East Sheen in German city

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters are taken from these words

explanation.surface: Some strange people from a London suburb have turned up in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: East Sheen is a district of south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Bad motion edit close to release delayed film

indicators.note: bad here means badly made, so the letters of these two words are reworked
the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A critic pans a film's sloppy editing, just before it finally comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' turns MOTION EDIT into NOTIMETODI, and 'close to' adds the E at the end of 'release'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2021 James Bond film had its cinema release postponed several times during the pandemic.

clue.text: Sooner or later does he say? Often that's nonsense

indicators.note: the words as given make nonsense, so their letters must be rearranged into sense

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man keeps saying he will do something eventually, calling it rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to some unspecified time in the future, meaning eventually.

clue.text: One remedy having answer for universal solitude

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: A for answer replaces U for universal, the film classification letter

parts.note: a solution is a remedy for a problem

explanation.surface: A single cure for everyone's loneliness is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having answer for universal' swaps the U of SOLUTION for A, giving SOLATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is the state of being alone, cut off from others, which is what solitude means.

clue.text: Urban district contained within barrier it has

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A town is enclosed by its own boundary wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Erith is a town in the London borough of Bexley, formerly an urban district in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Erith was administered as an urban district, the British term for a small town council area.

clue.text: One trapped in large marsh for slow absorption

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: the one is caught inside the marsh, so its letter sits within

parts.note: a moss is a bog or marsh, chiefly in northern Britain
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in a big bog, slowly sinking into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss in the sense of a peat bog is a northern English and Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the gradual passage of fluid through a membrane, and figuratively gradual unconscious absorption of ideas.

clue.text: Progressive splitting outside in-patient lavatory?

indicators.note: the splitting word goes outside, around the other pieces

parts.note: forking means dividing in two, splitting
an in-patient stays on a hospital ward
loo is British slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: Splitting a hospital toilet for in-patients from the outside is called progressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The splitting word breaks after its third letter to wrap around the rest; the surface's hyphen ties in-patient to lavatory, but it stands alone for the hospital room.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward-looking describes someone who plans for the future and favours modern ideas, as a progressive does.

clue.text: With which one sees stars become smaller

definitions.meaning: the instrument used to view stars
to shorten or contract by sections sliding into one another

explanation.surface: Stars seen through the instrument appear to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument's sliding tubes give the verb sense of collapsing into a shorter length.

clue.text: Number with hatred for decimalisation?

indicators.note: in British decimalisation in 1971 the old penny, d, gave way to the new penny, p, so a D becomes a P

parts.note: odium is general hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: A figure is linked with loathing of the switch to decimal currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that numbs. 'for decimalisation?' swaps D for P, as Britain's old pence (d) became new pence (p) in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic painkiller, so it is a numb-er, something that deadens feeling.

clue.text: Albanian yeoman keeps whichever is chosen

indicators.note: these words keep the answer, holding its letters inside them

explanation.surface: A farmer from Albania holds on to whatever is picked.
explanation.definitionFit: Any refers to one or some of a group without specifying which, so whichever one is selected.

clue.text: Reports latest bands crossing fine line

parts.note: the latest thing is new

indicators.note: the bands cross over the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: sashes are bands of cloth worn round the body
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: News arrives of the newest pop groups crossing a thin line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts F and L inside SASHES, giving SFLASHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsflashes are brief, urgent news reports interrupting normal broadcasting.

clue.text: Beetle, or small mobile home?

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a camper is a vehicle fitted out for living in

explanation.surface: Is that a beetle, or just a tiny caravan?
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a verb here: to beetle is to hurry along, and it also hints at the VW Beetle car beside a camper van.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to scurry about quickly, just as beetling off means hurrying away.

clue.text: Pagan woman that is seen on street in crowd

indicators.note: these letters go in the crowd, inside its word

parts.note: a press is a crowd or throng of people

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece seen on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A heathen woman is spotted on a road among a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a woman who performs rites in a non-Christian religion, so a pagan cleric.

clue.text: Contemptible male American gets around in love

indicators.note: the male American pair goes around the other pieces

parts.note: he refers to a male
US is short for American, as in the US
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A despicable American man sleeps around while claiming to be in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets around' means the first pair of pieces surrounds INO, made from 'in' and the O of 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means shockingly wicked, so deserving contempt.

clue.text: Complain open clothes will show boob

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: one word dresses around the other

parts.note: overt means done openly
to sigh can mean to complain or lament

explanation.surface: A wardrobe malfunction leaves someone grumbling that revealing clothes show too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb here, not garments. 'boob' means a blunder, not the body part the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a mistake made by failing to notice something, which is what a boob is in British slang.

clue.text: See 4
Elite soldiers police volunteers without aggression

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: part-time unpaid constables in British police forces are known for short by a plural word meaning extraordinary ones
force means violence or aggression

explanation.surface: Volunteer police officers are told to do their job without using force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but here has its old sense of outside. Special constables, or specials, are part-time unpaid volunteers in British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Special forces are highly trained military units used for the most demanding operations.

clue.text: Resolved to live permanently with duke

parts.note: to settle is to make a permanent home somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone has decided to put down roots alongside a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled question is one that has been decided and is no longer in dispute.

clue.text: Following on is straightforward

parts.note: since means following, after a point in time
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Coming after something is presented as simple and honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere person is frank and without pretence, so straightforward in manner.

clue.text: Knife cut drawn up over ambassador's brain

indicators.note: the reversed knife goes over the ambassador, so around his letters
in a down clue a word drawn up is read from bottom to top, backwards
a cut word loses its last letter

parts.note: a dagger is a short knife
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A blade is pulled up over an envoy's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the knife to DAGGE, 'drawn up' reverses that to EGGAD, and 'over' wraps it around the ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Brain is informal for a clever person, the same as an egghead, an intellectual.

clue.text: One leaving coaches to consider electrical device

indicators.note: one leaving means that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: trains are made up of coaches; to train is also to coach
one is the Roman numeral I
to ponder is to consider

explanation.surface: A person getting off the carriages stops to think about a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of TRAINS to give TRANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A transponder is a radio device that receives a signal and automatically transmits a reply.

clue.text: Two daughters introduced to beer become confused

indicators.note: the daughters are introduced into the beer, inside its letters

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
D is the abbreviation for daughter, so two give DD

explanation.surface: Two girls are given beer and start to lose their wits.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle, and also intransitively to grow muddled, as an egg goes bad.

clue.text: Old beak in female bird

definitions.meaning: a medieval local official or magistrate, beak being slang for a magistrate
the female of the ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: An ancient bill is found on a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The two senses are unrelated: a historic officer of law, and the name for a female ruff.

clue.text: Hang from gallows again?

indicators.note: the answer is taken from inside the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Is someone going to be hanged a second time?
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or hang down loosely.

clue.text: See BBC boss back to the Masonic premises

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
the head of the BBC is the Director-General, DG

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and see the BBC chief back at the Freemasons' hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's public broadcaster, run by a Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: A Masonic lodge is a local branch of Freemasons and the building where they meet.

clue.text: College group has three miles on climber

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A climbing plant has grown three miles long.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is a group of eight old, prestigious universities in the north-eastern US.

clue.text: Groom to get on as horse moves

parts.note: to groom is to dress, as hair or a horse
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: A stable hand gets on with the job while the horse moves about.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the trained performance of precise movements by a horse.

clue.text: Hit with a band?

definitions.meaning: to belt is to strike hard
wearing a belt, a band around the waist

explanation.surface: A musical hit, played with a group?
explanation.definitionFit: Belted means both struck forcefully and fitted with a belt.
